I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, that is the most steady way for me to use the full year, and at my age I care more about stability, labor I can handle, and cash coming back reliably than about trying fancy crops. So the winter wheat already in the ground stays, and after harvest I will go straight into summer maize on the same fields. I will use better seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want even stands and fewer problems. I will not make the field plan too scattered. I want simple management, mechanized work, and inputs I understand well.

For wheat, I will manage for stable yield, not extreme yield. I will put most fertilizer up front, then topdress nitrogen once at the jointing stage. I will irrigate at the key times instead of watering too often, because water costs money and too much water can push disease and weak plants. I will watch aphids, rust, and lodging risk, and spray only when the field pressure is there. For maize, after wheat harvest I will move fast, keep the stubble, and use no-tillage seeding so I save time and moisture. I will feed maize mainly with nitrogen, keep phosphorus and potassium moderate, and water around the big demand stages. I will keep pesticide use limited unless I see real insect or disease pressure. That is the plan I would follow because it matches the local climate, the land use pattern here, and the kind of risk I am willing to take.
